researchNotes: Original authors preserved on every retained pin. Reconciled all 24 stale local IDs against live title, source URL and author before mutation; immediately re-read each record before writing. The database restore means old posted-local IDs cannot be trusted.

Opened/read fresh MISO API and SPP active HTML tables. Read the valid August 2026 EIA workbook acquired earlier on the same research date; it is not a tracker derivative. Exact primary records: MISO J2377/J3840/J2716/J3843; SPP GEN-2025-SR16/GEN-2025-SR28/GEN-2024-170/GEN-2017-184/GEN-2024-338; PJM AF2-226/AF2-319 final studies released May 14, 2026.

Cleared 21 unsupported capital-cost estimates and five calculated energy rows in each environment. Removed fictional developer LLCs, unsourced four-hour MWh assumptions, construction assertions and unsupported grid voltages. Queue status and requested dates are not construction/operation evidence.

Silver Creek CEC TN 272831 was downloaded and read. Its 99 MW total load is separate from IT, whose figures conflict between 69.2 and 69.7 MW. The application supports 516,000 sqft, 15.13 acres, 44 backup generators, air-cooled chillers and estimated potable demand 8,700 gal/day. The pin dates the September 18, 2026 filing; proposed January 2028 construction and approximately 16-month duration are not a confirmed COD.

CENTRA current page and linked two-page tech sheet support 8.1 MW critical capacity, versus 12 MVA utility power. The sheet stages 3.6 MW Q4 2026 / 4.5 MW Q3 2027 and describes four generators installed plus four planned in 2027. The 2025 press release used 12 MW critical; the discrepancy is explicit. PUE/design values also differ and were not copied into native telemetry.

CoreSite current DE3 community page supports 4900 Race Street, approximately 170,000 sqft, 18 MW compute power, forecast 115,000 gal/day and late-2026 delivery target. Its operator timeline lists February 2025 permits and October 2025 groundbreaking. Regional investment/tax figures were not substituted for project capital cost.

RadiusDC current facility page distinguishes two 6 MW data halls / 12 MW critical from 20 MW building utility power; current floor area is rounded 102,000 sqft versus 102,500 in the 2025 release. The operator market page says opened in 2026 and fully leased; exact opening day remains unknown. The 2902 Brick Church Pike address is reproduced as a plaintiff allegation in the opened federal court memorandum, not a judicial finding of ownership or permit approval.

Ten location changes required 30 replacement USGS maps. Nottingham, Firefly, Mirasol, Sunfish and Elevate use EIA reporting points. Silver Creek and DE3 use Census-geocoded operator/filing addresses; CENTRA uses the linked tech-sheet Opperman address, alongside the website’s Nasseff Way label. Oak Run uses the Census SR38/SR29 intersection matching its site-plan context. Radius uses the geocoded court-record address, qualified as context.

Official gallery checks produced eight additional Azure assets: CENTRA exterior visualization, 2025 groundbreaking photograph and layout diagram; CoreSite DE3 concept rendering and historical pre-development concrete-plant photograph; Radius architectural rendering; Oak Run preliminary plan; Silver Creek CEC Figure 2.3-3 aerial-context diagram (underlying April 2024 Google Earth image). Full source URLs, credits and captions are recorded. None is presented as a current commissioning photograph.

Nottingham’s official page includes an Unsplash stock solar photo, rejected for pin use. Sunfish operator/Consumers pages had no additional verified project photograph adopted. Vesper/Firefly and Mirasol operator/filing searches did not yield a verified current project photo. Storage queue records lack project galleries; existing Top Crop/Balko wind photographs were not borrowed as battery evidence.

Chirisa’s official page was opened through web search despite plain HTTP returning a captcha interstitial. It supports only campus-wide 90 MW / 20-acre / reserved-2027 PNJ-01/02 scope; existing Piscataway overlap is queued, with shared URL kept exactly in references. No synthetic URL fragments or automatic record merges.

OPSB Oak Run case/news details are search-indexed but direct requests returned 404. The opened Savion project website independently confirms approval and links the downloaded preliminary project plan. The March 21, 2024 approval date comes from the OPSB announcement; current commissioning is unverified.

Sumner’s published Resolution 2026-03 was opened as a primary legal-notice PDF via web despite a local requests timeout. Its unincorporated-area moratorium does not establish that Oxford GEN-2025-SR16 itself was denied or lies in county rather than municipal jurisdiction. Verify later amendments and exact parcel before inferring an effect.

Firefly’s EIA entry is not a resolution of its historic interconnection dispute. The opened PJM December 2024 legal report is a party’s waiver-opposition position, not a FERC disposition. SPP GEN-2017-184’s reported Kansas county versus Nashua–St. Joe/KCPL location inconsistency remains explicit. Sunfish’s stale April/Q2-2026 operator targets conflict with EIA December 2026; neither proves actual operation.

Three held records have specific identity/split gaps: Meta Kuna Building 3 is not substantiated by a campus-wide opening; Vantage CO21 Building 1 is not substantiated by temporary-feeder documents or campus reports; Project Apollo Lakeland is not substantiated by a confidential Miami-Dade proposal. Soft-deleted on both environments and moved to held, not declared cancelled.

All fresh pin, power, datacenter and energy read-backs, current Azure files and retained native pin pages verified. Both posted maps contain 1,415 entries. No application code change, commit, deployment, restart or production build. Credit balance is not exposed; work stopped at a fully verified 24-pin checkpoint.
